reason: In free template outerNormal only `dir` (const short_t dir = s.direction()) is in scope; `!dim` names nothing (no namespace-scope dim in gismo at 6003fdf, md.dim is a member), so GCC rejects the non-dependent name.
In elementIndex the loop variable is `i`; m_bases[j] uses an undeclared non-dependent name (gsTensorBasis.h has no member j), which GCC rejects.
The new 4-argument matchWith forwards `bb`, which is only a local inside boundaryBasis; the parameter is `bi`. It is an undeclared non-dependent name, and no member bb exists.

_pattern::push takes row actives from the column space u instead of v, while still using rowMap = v.mapper(). For mixed spaces (v != u) the sparsity pattern gets wrong row indices. The in-tree caller poisson2_example uses u*u and is unaffected.

toBoxes uses `i = 2` instead of `i += 2`, so every element after the first overwrites columns 2-3. gsElementHelper::toBoxes is explicitly instantiated but never called: examples call gsHElementHelper::toBoxes.

updateBdr rebuilds m_masterBdr from bi.first() (the slave side) on the master geometry, but the constructor uses bi.second(). gsExprAssembler calls interfaceMap.updateBdr() in the moving-interface Jacobian loop, so the wrong boundary is used there.

In gsMultiPatch::coefs(), `offset = coefsSize()` instead of `+=` makes every patch after the second write at the previous patch's size. Blocks overlap, the last rows stay zero and the assembled coefficient matrix is wrong.

In asElementsUnrefine, k2's upper_bound range drops the +1 (domainUEnd() instead of domainUEnd()+1). A box ending at the domain end gets k2 one knot short, so the unrefinement box misses the last element. refine() and the removed line use +1.

m = n/2 is a declared const unsigned, so it compiles, but the Newton initial guess uses m+0.5 instead of n+0.5. For n=2 the start is x=0, where dpn=0 and the update divides by zero; in general the guess converges to wrong or duplicate roots. computeReference runs when lookup fails or digits != 0.

pruned(Scalar tol) passes `col` to scalar_prune_op. MatrixBase does not `using Base::col` (DenseBase is a dependent base), so `col` is an undeclared non-dependent name that GCC rejects at definition. pruned() itself has no dense caller in-tree.

deriv2Single_into mixed-derivative row c gets an extra cwiseProduct(ev[l]) because r starts at l instead of l+1, so the result is wrong. The 0..k, k+1..l, l+1..d product pattern is visible in the hunk.

In blockTransposeInPlace's nr==colBlock branch, `i` is undeclared because it is only declared later in the else branch, so the build fails. Had it compiled, the wrong block would be transposed. The function is called from gsFunction.hpp:48 and gsTHBSplineBasis.hpp.

BiCGStab step overwrites the iterate (`x = alpha*y + w*z`) instead of accumulating it while the residual is still updated incrementally, so the solution is wrong. That is evident from the algorithm in the shown file.

The non-periodic consistency check drops the +1, so #coefs+deg+1==#knots no longer holds: it warns for every valid B-spline built from a knot vector and stays silent for bad ones. Only the diagnostic is affected, not the geometry. The removed line in the diff shows the +1.

computeReference sets x[0]=-1, then the plant overwrites it with 1e-12 (the mid-interval) instead of nudging it by +1e-12, so a quadrature node is wrong. The asymmetry with `x[n-1] -= 1e-12` is visible in the diff.

update_structure resizes m_xmatrix to getMaxInsLevel() instead of +1, which drops the finest level's characteristic matrix and its active functions. needLevel(getMaxInsLevel()) and the needLevel body ('+1 for the initial basis') in the same hunk show that levels are 0-based and inclusive.

beginBdr's parameter is `bs`, but the plant writes GISMO_UNUSED(bi) (static_cast<void>(bi)), and bi is undeclared there. gsDomain.h is included by gsAssembler.h, gsExprAssembler.h and others, so the build breaks. The runtime semantics would be unchanged (the stub throws anyway).

In _computePatternIfc (called from assembleIfc), the end iterator is basis1.domain()->endBdr(iFace.second().side()). It sets the end at numElementsBdr of the wrong side of patch1, so iteration skips elements or overruns when the sides have different element counts. beginBdr uses first().side().

getHNeighborhood uses level lvl-m instead of lvl-m+1 (the H-neighbourhood definition), giving a too-coarse support extension and a wrong admissible-refinement neighbourhood. It is reached from getNeighborhood for HB-splines via gsHElementMarker. The sibling getTNeighborhood (lvl-m+2) and the removed line show the convention.
BSplineCube overwrites the x column with x+0.5 instead of adding to the scaled coefficients, so all control points share one x coordinate and the cube is degenerate. The y and z lines use +=.
In uniformSplit, m_patches[mp] uses `mp` before `gsMultiPatch<T> mp(result)` is declared below, and there is no member `mp`, so the build fails. The loop variable is np.

splitAtMult starts at ubegin(), whose boundary knot has multiplicity p+1>=minMult, so it splits at the domain start and produces a degenerate piece. However, splitAtMult has no caller anywhere in the repo at this commit (git grep finds only its own declaration, definition and recursion).

GISMO_ASSERT(maxInteriorMultiplicity()<degree()) now rejects interior multiplicity p, which is legal and contradicts the message 'higher than p'. addLevel is called from nestedTHB_example and poissonTHB_example, so Debug builds throw; Release compiles the assert away.
getBasename's separator-only branch returns fn.substr(pos1), so the result keeps the leading '/' or '\'. The neighbouring code uses pos1+1 (the extension branch and getFilename).

coupling holds pair(k, localIndex), so .first is the patch number. localMappedIndex1 = coupling[i][j1].first puts the patch id in as a column of the jump matrix, while the j2 branch correctly uses .second.

`const bool fc = (0==fclose(fc));` passes the bool being declared to fclose(FILE*). There is no bool-to-FILE* conversion, and the expression is non-dependent, so the build breaks (fr is never closed either).

eval returns `_u.eval(k) > 0 ? _u.eval(k) : _w.eval(k)`. For the space-valued use at line 435 (ternary(m_eps - jac(G).det(), -derJacDet, space1*zeroVar)) _u yields a Scalar and _w an Eigen matrix with no implicit conversion between them. gsObjFoldoverFree<d,real_t>::gradObj_into is instantiated via gsBarrierCore<2/3,real_t>, so this fails to compile; in the scalar uses it would return the condition value. The commented original line shows _v.
bb is a local of boundaryBasis, not of matchWith(const boundaryInterface & bi, ...). m_src->matchWith(bb, ...) names an undeclared identifier, and bi goes unused.
`for (k = m_offset[h]; k < m_offset[h]; ++k)` never executes, so assembleSystem adds no point contributions and the multipatch fit solves an empty system.
repairInterface refines patch bi.second().patch with refEltsFirst, which are element indices of the first patch. The first patch is never repaired and the second gets wrong elements.
addLine(v0,v1,midPts) places point i at start+i*h*step, so the first midpoint coincides with v0 (zero-length edge) and the last segment is twice as long. Called from gsMesh.hpp:107 and gsIOUtils.h.

cf.pop_back() comes before `gsMatrix<T> cf(...)` is declared in the same function. The undeclared non-dependent name fails in the explicitly instantiated gsTensorBSpline. The intended removal of cv's doubled last point is also lost.

The basis is evaluated up to order m=domainDim() instead of the requested n, while evals[i] is read for i<=n. For gsMappedSpline<1,real_t> (instantiated in gsMappedSpline_.cpp) with n=2, evals[2] is out of bounds. For 2D and 3D the planted code only does extra work.
ins is std::pair<map::iterator,bool>, so ins.second->second applies -> to a bool. The virtual piece() is instantiated through gsFunction<T>::coord(), which builds a gsFuncCoordinate<T>.

The inner loop bound uses other.m_face[j] instead of m_face[i]. A copy of a mesh with fewer faces than vertices per face indexes past m_face, and faces with different vertex counts copy the wrong number of vertices.

step() pushes beta/alpha into m_delta, and the Lanczos diagonal needs 1/alpha added to it. Assigning 1/alpha discards the beta/alpha part, so the condition number is wrong when it is computed before convergence (m_error >= m_tol). The push_back(beta/alpha) is visible in the diff context.
With sorted=true the vertex is fetched with getVertex(i+1) but i is returned, an off-by-one. gsParametrization.h:378 calls findVertex(...,true).
operator-(typename E::Scalar const& s, _expr<E> const& v) has no `u`, so the undeclared non-dependent name is an error at template definition (GCC). It should pass v.
ElementBlocks[key].numElements = 1 overwrites the count instead of incrementing it (the comment says Increment), so a block with several elements reports 1 while actives and coefVectors keep growing.
The loop `k < m_offset[h]` starting at k = m_offset[h] never runs, so m_pointErrors stays empty. computeMaxNormErrors() is called from examples/gsMakeMultiPatch.cpp.
ab << t1, t1 collapses the interval [t1,t2] to a point, so the 1D gsPointGrid(t1,t2,n) returns n copies of t1.
boundaryBasis_impl declares bb (the uPtr) but uses bi.release(), and no `bi` is in scope in this function (bi is only a parameter of matchWith). The name is undeclared.

getSpace(const gsFunctionSet<T>&, ...) accepts the mutable gsMultiPatch m_mp, so it compiles, but the FE space is built from the geometry instead of the basis m_mb, which does not match m_mapper. gsBarrierCore<2|3,real_t> instantiates gsObjFoldoverFree.

outerNormal declares only `dir` (const short_t dir = s.direction()); bare `dim` is undeclared there (only md.dim exists), so `md.jacobian(k).col(!dim)` fails to compile; outerNormal is called from gsVisitorNeumann/Nitsche/Dg, so it is instantiated.

In elementIndex the loop variable is `i`; `m_bases[j]` uses an undeclared non-dependent `j`, so GCC rejects it at definition. elementIndex is virtual in gsBasis (gsBasis.h:772), so it is instantiated anyway.

The new 4-arg matchWith passes `bb`, which is declared only as a local in boundaryBasis; the parameter is `bi`. The undeclared non-dependent name is an error, and the virtual matchWith (gsBasis.h:983) is instantiated with the class.

_pattern::push takes the row actives from the column space u (`u.source()...active`) while rd and rowMap come from v. For mixed or differing row/column spaces the interface sparsity pattern gets wrong or missing row entries. It is harmless only when u==v.

In gsElementHelper::toBoxes, `i = 2` instead of `i += 2` makes every box after the second overwrite columns 2-3, a real logic bug. But git grep at c99ef24 finds no caller of gsElementHelper::toBoxes: the examples call gsHElementHelper::toBoxes, which uses toBoxesAndLevels, and the class is only explicitly instantiated.

updateBdr sets m_masterBdr from m_masterGeom->boundary(bi.first()), the slave side, while the constructor uses bi.second(). updateBdr is called five times in gsExprAssembler.h, so closest-point projection uses the wrong boundary.

In gsMultiPatch::coefs(), `offset = coefsSize()` instead of `+=` places patch k at the previous patch's size rather than the running sum. With 3 or more patches the blocks overlap and the rows near the end stay zero.

asElementsUnrefine now searches k2 with upper_bound over [domainUBegin, domainUEnd) instead of domainUEnd()+1. domainUEnd points at the last knot (gsKnotVector.h:54), so boxes ending at the domain end get k2 one too small. The function is called from gsAdaptiveMeshing and gsAdaptiveRefUtils.

The Newton initial guess uses cos(pi*(i+0.75)/(m+0.5)) with m = n/2 instead of n. The starting points become wrong for the degree-n Legendre polynomial, so Newton can converge to wrong or duplicate roots, giving wrong Gauss nodes and weights. The removed line shows n.

pruned(Scalar tol) passes `col` (DenseBase::col, from a dependent base, not visible to unqualified lookup) instead of `tol`. GCC and Clang reject the undeclared name at definition; lenient MSVC would defer the error. The dense MatrixBase::pruned has no caller at b5cc7e6 (only sparse .pruned in Eigen docs), so the bug never runs.

In deriv2Single_into the mixed-derivative row is already multiplied by dev[l]. Starting at r=l multiplies it again by ev[l], so the result is wrong. The neighbouring loops skip k and l, which shows the pattern. gsTensorBasis is explicitly instantiated.

In blockTransposeInPlace's `nr == colBlock` branch only `j` is in scope (`i` is declared later, in the else branch), so `middleCols(i,colBlock)` names an undeclared non-dependent identifier inside the gsMatrix template.

`x.noalias() = m_alpha*m_y + m_w*m_z` overwrites the iterate with the update instead of adding it, while the residual is still decremented with `-=`. The solution is therefore wrong after the first step.

Dropping the +1 inverts the consistency check #coefs+deg+1==#knots: every valid non-periodic gsBSpline(KV,coefs) prints a spurious gsWarn, and off-by-one inputs are no longer reported. Only diagnostics change, not numbers. The removed line in the diff shows the +1.

computeReference sets x[0] = -1, so `x[0] = 1e-12` moves the first node to ~0 instead of -1+1e-12, breaking the quadrature nodes. The appended function body shows x[0] = -1 and the symmetric `x[n-1] -= 1e-12`.

update_structure calls needLevel(getMaxInsLevel()), which makes level index maxIns valid, so there are maxIns+1 levels. Resizing m_xmatrix to getMaxInsLevel() drops the finest level's active functions. The removed line resized to m_bases.size().
beginBdr's parameter is `bs`. GISMO_UNUSED(bi) expands to static_cast<void>(bi) with `bi` undeclared in the gsDomain<T> template. gsDomain.h is included by gsAssembler.h and others.
In the interface assembly loop domIt starts at beginBdr(first side) but domItEnd = endBdr(second side), so the element range is mismatched. The begin/end pair is visibly inconsistent in the diff.

getHNeighborhood uses k = lvl - m + 1 (the H-neighbourhood level); `lvl - m` takes the support extension one level too coarse, so the neighbourhood is wrong for admissible marking. gsHElementHelper<2,3> is instantiated and getNeighborhood dispatches to it. The removed line shows +1.
BSplineCube(r,x,y,z): `C.col(0).array() = x + 0.5` overwrites all x-coordinates with a constant, which degenerates the cube. The y/z lines still use +=.

In uniformSplit(index_t dir) the loop variable is `np`. `mp` is declared only after the loop (gsMultiPatch<T> mp(result)) and is not a member of gsMultiPatch/gsBoxTopology, so m_patches[mp] does not compile.

splitAtMult now iterates from ubegin(), the domain start knot of multiplicity p+1 >= minMult, so it calls splitAt at the boundary and pushes a degenerate piece; the loop already excludes the end knot via uend()-1. It is a public method of the explicitly instantiated class, but at this commit it has no caller in the repo besides its own recursion.

GISMO_ASSERT(maxInteriorMultiplicity()<degree()) rejects valid multiplicity p (and every degree-1 basis with interior knots) in debug builds; addLevel is used by poissonTHB_example --manual and nestedTHB_example. The message 'higher than p' contradicts the condition.
name = fn.substr(pos1) keeps the separator, so getBasename("dir/foo") returns "/foo". The other branch and getFilename both use pos1+1.
localMappedIndex1 = coupling[i][j1].first takes the patch index (patch1 is the line above) instead of the local dof .second, so jump matrices get wrong column indices; the j2 line uses .second.
fclose(fc) passes the const bool being initialized instead of FILE* fr; bool does not convert to FILE*, and the file would not be closed.

eval returns _u.eval(k) (the condition) instead of _v.eval(k). In gsObjFoldoverFree::gradObj_into (virtual, instantiated at line 323), ternary(m_eps - det, -derJacDet, space1*zeroVar) mixes a scalar with a matrix in ?:, and gsMatrix has no scalar constructor. The scalar uses (chi) would return eps-det. The commented line above shows _v.
'bb' is a local of boundaryBasis, not in scope in matchWith (parameter bi), so it is an undeclared identifier.
k < m_offset[h] is never true, so assembleSystem (called at gsFitting.hpp:94 for mapped fitting) assembles nothing and the system stays empty.

refEltsFirst (elements of the first patch from repairInterfaceFindElements) is refined on bi.second().patch, so the second patch is refined with the wrong element list and the first never; the removed code used first().
With h = len/(midPts+1) and i starting at 0, the first midpoint coincides with v0 and the last gap is 2h. addLine(v0,v1,midPts) is used in gsMesh.hpp:107 and gsIOUtils.h.

`cf.pop_back()` uses `cf` one line before `gsMatrix<T> cf(...)` is declared, so GCC rejects the non-dependent name at definition. gsMatrix also has no pop_back, and the list `cv` keeps its doubled last point.

m = domainDim() is passed instead of the derivative order n to gsMappedBasis::evalAllDers_into(index_t patch, const gsMatrix&, index_t n, vector&, bool). For gsMappedSpline<1,real_t> (instantiated in gsMappedSpline_.cpp) with n=2, evals has only 2 entries and evals[2] is out of bounds.
`ins` is pair<map::iterator,bool>, so `ins.second->second` applies -> to a bool. The virtual piece() is instantiated through gsFunction<T>::coord(), which constructs gsFuncCoordinate<T>.

The inner bound uses `other.m_face[j]->vertices.size()` (face j) instead of face i. With a single triangle, m_face[1] is read out of bounds; with mixed tri/quad faces the copy loop uses the wrong vertex count.

getConditionNumber before convergence replaces the last Lanczos diagonal with 1/alpha instead of adding it (step() does `m_delta.back()+=(1./alpha)`), so the condition number is wrong. The += in step() is not in the shown context, only the save/restore hints at it.
In sorted mode the loop uses getVertex(i+1) (1-based), but the function now returns i, one less. gsParametrization.h:378 calls findVertex(...,true) and gets off-by-one vertex indices.
operator-(Scalar s, _expr<E> const& v) returns sub_expr<...>(_expr(s), u), but `u` is not a parameter of this function, so the non-dependent name fails at definition. The variable meant is v.

`ElementBlocks[key].numElements = 1` resets the count, which the comment says should be incremented, so every block reports 1 element while actives/coefVectors keep growing. gsMultiPatch.hpp's twin uses `+= 1`.
`k < m_offset[h]` starting at k = m_offset[h] never runs, so computeMaxNormErrors computes no point errors and leaves m_max_error/m_min_error unset.
`ab << t1, t1` makes the interval [t1,t1], so the 1D gsPointGrid(t1,t2,n) returns n copies of t1 and ignores t2.
boundaryBasis_impl calls `bi.release()`, but only `bb` (the uPtr) is declared there (`bi` is a parameter of matchWith), so the non-dependent undeclared name is a compile error.

getSpace(const gsFunctionSet<T>&, index_t) accepts the gsMultiPatch m_mp, so it compiles. But the FE space then uses the geometry instead of the basis m_mb (which the removed line and the sibling functions use), so the gradient space and mapper do not match.

intervals[j][j] writes row j (j up to numInt, while intervals has only d rows), so it goes out of bounds and leaves intervals[i] unfilled. uniformIntervals is explicitly instantiated in gsPointGrid_.cpp. Both indices are int, so it compiles.
Only a Doxygen comment changes: the formula now reads 'j = 1..S' instead of 'i = 1..S'. The doc is wrong but nothing changes at runtime.

In matchWith, bndThis = this->boundaryOffset(bi.second().side(), offset) takes this patch's DOFs from the other patch's side. Interface matching for hierarchical bases (called from gsMultiBasis::matchInterface) then pairs the wrong DOFs. The side type is the same, so it compiles.

_knotIndexToDiadicIndex(fLevel,k2) is now called twice and k1 is never converted, so in refine() with m_manualLevels (set through the gsHTensorBasis(tbasis, manualLevels) constructor) the box lower corner stays in knot indices and k2 is converted twice. The overload (index_t, gsVector<index_t,d>&) exists.

gsConjugateGradient starts m_delta at size 1 with m_gamma empty and pushes one entry to each per step, so delta.size()==gamma.size()+1 always holds. In debug builds the new GISMO_ASSERT therefore throws on every getConditionNumber/getEigenvalues call. The class comment (tridiagonal, n diagonal and n-1 off-diagonal entries) and the gamma[i<n-1] loop show the intended relation.

k1 is declared as index_t a few lines above, so k1.size() asks for a member of a non-class type. asElementsUnrefine is a virtual member of the explicitly instantiated gsHTensorBasis and is used by gsAdaptiveRefUtils/gsAdaptiveMeshing, so the build breaks.

numColNz now computes bdB*deg+bdB instead of bdA*deg+bdB (defaults: deg+1 per direction instead of 2deg+1). bdA is ignored and gsAssembler::reserve under-allocates, which causes reallocation during assembly. Results stay correct; the cost is performance only. The doc comment in the shown hunk says bdA*deg + bdB.

The three-argument constructor clones x twice and drops y, which is a wrong 3D tensor basis. git grep finds no use of gsGenericTensorBasis outside its header and the include in gismo.h, so the class is never instantiated. The types are all Basis_t*, so it would compile if instantiated.

In the both-unsigned branch, util::less returns t2<t2, which is always false. The only in-repo callers (gsBasis.hpp:409/411, util::greater/less with an index_t and an unsigned) use mixed signedness, so this branch is compiled but never executed.

The attribute filter now tests the value instead of the key. Every caller passes either {"",""} or a fixed or checked-nonempty Name label (gsParaviewUtils.hpp:63-66, 97-101), so the output is identical. Only the header's expression overload with an empty label would drop Name="".

Changing the guard from size()>2p+1 to size()>2p only changes behaviour when exactly 2p+1 knots exist, a degenerate knot vector with no valid domain. Whether trimming there matters in practice (for example, incremental insertion into an unclamped vector) is unclear.

matchDofs(first.patch, b1, second.patch, b1, i) matches the first patch's interface indices with themselves on the second patch, so b2 is ignored. Every conforming getMapper on a multipatch couples the wrong DOFs.

b_const_iter is a typedef local to boundary(); innerBoundaries only declares i_const_iter, so the name is undeclared. gsMappedBasis<1..3,real_t> is explicitly instantiated, so the build breaks. innerBoundaries itself has no callers in the repo.

After a non-null block, apply() sets inputIndex = m_blockInputPositions(j) instead of adding it, so with three or more block columns the input slices are taken at wrong offsets. The null-block path still uses +=.
Only the step number in a gsDebug log line changes (i instead of i+1). It does not affect the computation.
'std::vector<T> knots2, knots2;' is a local redeclaration, which GCC and Clang reject even in an uninstantiated template. isNested is never called anywhere (git grep) and both vectors are unused.

In gsTraceLine, Jmap.row(1) uses map.first, which gives a singular Jacobian (det 0, so the Newton iteration breaks immediately). gsTraceLine is a free function template with no caller (gsTraceCurve.hpp is only included by gsPlanarDomain.hpp), so it is never instantiated.

The fine knot count uses fkv.firstKnotIndex(clow[dim]), a coarse-level index on the fine knot vector, which breaks the symmetry with the cnmb line. _updateSizeOfCoefs is called at gsTHBSplineBasis.hpp:155/183 when computing THB coefficients, so the coefficient sizes come out wrong.

In toMesh, m_loops[i] uses the y-sample index i (0..yPoints) instead of the loop index j, so it evaluates the wrong loop or reads out of bounds. toMesh is reached via gsTrimSurface::toMesh and gsWriteParaview.

gsKnotVector<T>(0,1,0,ElBlock.PS) gives the Bezier patch degree PS-1 in v, so it no longer matches the (PR+1)(PS+1) extracted coefficients. extractBezier runs from gsParaviewUtils.hpp:208, and the removed line kv2(0,1,0,ElBlock.PS+1) is shown in the diff.
In the combineCorners branch i==0, so last.push_back(it->second[i]) pushes the first corner component nrcp times instead of each it->second[j]. multiGrid_example calls allComponents(true).

`get` is not declared in scope (the parameter is `geo`). It is a non-dependent name, so GCC rejects it at template definition, and the header is included by gsFitting.h and others. Had it compiled, the scaled coefs would never be written back.

new gsTensorBSpline<2,T>(ckv, ckv, ...) uses the v knot vector in u, which builds a wrong patch. gsTHBSplineBasis<2,real_t> is explicitly instantiated, but getBsplinePatchesToMultiPatch has no caller in the repo (public API only).
In patchSide(patch, size, name), `size` is not a local; the local is `side`. Even if a std::size were visible, it cannot convert to boxSide, and gsXml.cpp is non-template library code.
Unary operator-(_expr<E1> const& u) returns mult_expr(-1, v), and no `v` is declared. It is a non-dependent unqualified name, so GCC errors at definition, and unary minus is widely used anyway.

h=(u1-u0)/T(interior) puts the last interior knot at u1, which wrongly raises the end multiplicity. initGraded has no caller in the repo, and gsKnotVector is not class-instantiated (gsKnotVector_.cpp only instantiates gsXml<gsKnotVector>).
The constructor sets target(v0), so every edge is degenerate (source==target). It is used by gsMesh<T>::addEdge -> Edge(v0,v1), and the `sharp` member exists at the commit.
swap() renames parrays_[spair.second] twice, so the first property keeps name1 and the second also ends up as name1. It is called through gsSurfMesh::swap_vertex_property (examples/cc_surf.cpp).
starts_with never advances it2 and steps it1 by 2, so it compares only needle[0], can step past haystack.end() (out of bounds), and returns wrong results. gsOptionList.cpp calls it.

gsQuadrature::numNodes takes only (const gsBasis<T>&, Real, index_t, short_t) or (const gsDomain<T>&, ...), and ab is a gsMatrix<T>. gsQuasiInterpolate<real_t> is explicitly instantiated in gsQuasiInterpolate_.cpp.
GISMO_UNUSED(b2) twice leaves b1 unmarked, which only causes an unused-parameter warning. The body is GISMO_NO_IMPLEMENTATION, so there is no behavioural difference.

addCornerValue(boxCorner c, T value, int p, short_t unknown, int component) is called with pIndex as the component instead of cIndex (default -1), so corner values from XML get a wrong component, and cIndex is left unused.
`gsMatrix<T> m_box2, m_box2;` redeclares a member, which is an error at class template definition. It also drops m_box1, which the gsAffineFunction.hpp constructor initializes.
m_ops[1]=give(op0) after op0 was already moved, so m_ops[1] is a null shared_ptr and op1 is dropped, a null dereference on apply. gsProductOp is never instantiated or used anywhere in the repo.

globProjRhs.at(ii) = ... overwrites the quadrature/element accumulation instead of +=, which gives a wrong L2-projection RHS. gsDirichletValuesByL2Projection runs for dirichlet::l2Projection (poisson2_example, linear_elasticity_example).
With l=k the inner loop writes d extra entries, so prm[m] goes out of bounds for sz=d(d+1)/2. deriv2lex_inplace has no caller, and gsFuncData is not class-instantiated, so it is never instantiated.

res[i] uses the face index i (the function parameter) instead of the loop index j, so one wrong entry is written (out of bounds when i >= nverts) and the rest stay uninitialized. gsMesh<real_t> is instantiated, and gsWriteOpenNurbs.hpp calls faceIndices.

coefL and coefR are both gsMatrix<T>, so it compiles. The right half of splitAt gets the left half's coefficients: wrong geometry, or a size mismatch whenever nL != nR. splitAt is reached through uniformSplit and gsMultiPatch::uniformSplit.

Inside the loop d<dim, `d != dim` is always true, so the boundary coordinate is never set to supp(d,0/1) and `dir` is left unused. parameterCenter(boxSide) is non-virtual and is used by gsMultiPatch::parameterCenter(ps) and by computeAuxiliaryData.

`it = (lvl==0?1:2)` assigns an int to typename gsKnotVector<T>::uiterator. gsUKnotIterator has only explicit constructors from a knot vector and no int assignment. reduceContinuity overrides the virtual gsBasis::reduceContinuity, so it is instantiated, and even if it compiled the loop would not advance.

In the else branch, `degreeReduce(j)` uses j, which is declared only in the for loop of the if branch. The non-dependent name is undeclared, so GCC rejects it at definition, and the virtual override is instantiated anyway.

out.dim.second is assigned twice and dim.first (ParDim, per the gsFuncData.h comment) is never set, so it keeps a stale or uninitialized value. The jacobian and hessian accessors of gsFuncData use dim.first.
gsVector3d<T>(y,y,z) drops the x coordinate: every vertex built from three scalars gets x=y.
math::min(3,pDim) compiles (int, int), but tmp has gDim rows. A surface in 3D (pDim=2, gDim=3) loses its z coordinate in evaluateMesh, and the removed line used gDim.
numColNz now multiplies by (1+bdA) instead of the documented (1+bdO) overhead. That only changes the reserve() estimate (over-allocation), not the assembled result.
The x offset uses j instead of i, so patches with different i coincide and the grid overlaps. BSplineCubeGrid is instantiated and exported to Python (gsNurbsCreator_.cpp def_static).
`at->side()`: no variable `at` exists in computeDirichletDofsIntpl or in gsAssembler (the loop iterator is `it`), so the non-dependent undeclared name fails to compile.

The parameter is renamed `map`, but the body still uses `mat`, which is undeclared (the class member is m_mat and the base is dependent). GCC errors at definition time, even though make() has no callers at this commit.

The sameElement branch of linearCombination_into uses `=` instead of `+=`, so only the last active function or component contributes. The path is reached via gsGeometry::evalAllDers_into(sameElement) from gsFunctionSet::compute with SAME_ELEMENT.
addShift sets m_shift instead of adding to it (its name and setShift above show the intent), but git grep finds no caller of addShift at 1f81f25.
m_end(point1) gives a zero-length segment: direction() is 0 and intersectSegment always returns false. It is used in gsParametrization.hpp:616 (gsLineSegment<2,T> actualLine).
mult = p - multiplicity inserts the knot only up to multiplicity p, while the comment and the removed line require p+1. The coefficient and knot split in splitAt is then wrong.
`rows = m_localRhs[k].rows()` overwrites instead of accumulating, so result is too small and the later middleRows(i,l) goes out of bounds. rhsForSaddlePoint is called in examples/ieti2_example.cpp.

cNew is a scalar T member (gsMinimalResidual.h:105, assigned a0/a1 in the same function), so cNew.col(0) is invalid. The class is explicitly instantiated in gsMinimalResidual_.cpp (CLASS_TEMPLATE_INST gsMinimalResidual<real_t>).
The member declaration now lists cr2 twice (a redeclaration) and drops cr1, which gsMinResQLP.hpp uses 8 times. The class is instantiated in gsMinResQLP_.cpp.
addTo(i,j,val) now assigns instead of adding, contradicting its own doc comment, but git grep 'addTo(' at 5178660 finds no caller in src or the rest of gismo (only Eigen's unrelated addTo).

gsFileData::getId<Object>(const int & id) gets the static member function clang instead of the int _lang. The function does not convert to const int&, and load() is a non-template inline member of a struct included from gismo.h, so the error is always hit.
degreeElevate(short_t i, short_t dir) has no j in scope. An undeclared non-dependent name is a compile error, and gsBSpline<real_t> is instantiated anyway.

Using it+p instead of it+p+1 picks a span inside [t_j, t_{j+p}] (or [t_j, next knot] when the difference is 0), which is still in the support of function j. The gsBasis.h contract only asks for 'an element in the support'. Only the middle choice changes, and only for odd p.

The posit nextafter overload declares parameter y twice (an ill-formed declaration even without instantiation) and its body uses an undeclared x. It sits under #ifdef gsUniversal_ENABLED, so it is compiled only with the optional Universal library and is excluded from the default build.
constructBoundaryRep declares only p1, so p2.boundary(*it) uses an undeclared non-dependent name, and gsMultiPatch<real_t> is explicitly instantiated.

push(v,u,index_t ra,index_t ca) gets ra for the column offset in the m_elim (default true) branch. When the row space is SAME_ELEMENT but the column space is not, the column offset is 0 instead of k, unlike the else branch, which passes ra, ca.

_knotIndexToDiadicIndex(const index_t level, const index_t dir, index_t&) receives the box index i as the direction for k1, while k2 uses j. With manualLevels=true (a constructor option) the wrong or out-of-range direction is used.
m_f1 is bound to f2, so eval_into computes |f2(u)-f2(geo(u))| or 0 instead of the error between f1 and f2. gsAbsError is used by gsFieldCreator::absError.
'index_t i, i;' redeclares i, and j (used in 'for ( j = 2; ...') is never declared. Both are compile errors at definition.

solveUpperTriangular assigns to x, which is neither a member (the members are tmp, g, g_tmp, h_tmp, y, w...) nor a parameter. The undeclared non-dependent name fails to compile, and y, which gsGMRes.hpp reads after solveUpperTriangular(H, g_tmp), would never be set.
x = step_size * m_update overwrites the iterate instead of updating it, while m_res -= step_size*m_tmp still assumes an increment. Residual and iterate diverge, and the method stops converging.
bndThis takes this->boundaryOffset(bi.second().side(), offset), the side of the other patch, so matchWith couples the wrong boundary DOFs whenever the two interface sides differ.

it=4 assigns an int to std::vector<gsVertex<T>*>::const_iterator, which has no such conversion. writeSingleBasisMesh2D is instantiated through writeSingleBasisMesh, which is called from gsWriteParaview(gsBasis<T>,...), and that is TEMPLATE_INST in gsWriteParaview_.cpp.

visitedSides is std::vector<patchSide>, while pcNeighbour is a patchCorner. patchSide has only 0- and 2-argument constructors and patchCorner has no conversion to patchSide, so push_back fails in this non-template .cpp. The value would also be stale at that point.

makeMatrix(it, n, m) allocates n x n instead of n x m. The callers gsHTensorBasis::allBoundary and boundaryOffset pass m=1, so they get an n x n matrix whose extra columns are uninitialized, with wrong cols() and size().

seg1 = seg compares a segment with itself, so currentPt is always line[seg]'s first point and index[] records seg instead of the next segment. identifyCycle then finds the wrong shared vertex and breakCycles splits the polylines wrongly.

invertPoints(pr, tmp, accuracy) inverts the patch's parameter range instead of the query point pt (both are gsMatrix<T>), so locatePoints returns wrong pids and preimages. pt is computed but never used.

intervals[j][j] with int j is well-typed; uniformIntervals is TEMPLATE_INST'd in gsPointGrid_.cpp (exported, no in-tree caller). It writes the diagonal of the outer vector (out of bounds once j>=d) and leaves intervals[i] unset.
The change is inside a Doxygen comment: the index text reads 'j = 1..S' instead of 'i = 1..S'. The documentation is wrong, but no code changes.

bndThis = this->boundaryOffset(bi.second().side(), offset) takes this basis's DOFs on the other patch's side. The loop then treats them as first()-side functions, so matchWith (used by gsMultiBasis::matchInterface) produces wrong interface matches.

_knotIndexToDiadicIndex(fLevel,k2) is called twice, and the overload takes gsVector<index_t,d> as k1 does. With m_manualLevels, k1 stays a knot index while k2 is converted, so sinkBox gets mixed index systems (k2 is converted twice).

gsConjugateGradient builds m_delta with one more entry than m_gamma (resize(1,0) and then paired push_backs), so the assert delta.size()==gamma.size() always fails in debug builds. Condition-number and eigenvalue requests then abort; the class doc (n diagonal, n-1 off-diagonal) shows this.
k1 is declared in the shown code as index_t (a non-dependent scalar), so k1.size() is an ill-formed member access in this compiled function. The intended bound was kv.size().

bdB (index_t) * T is well-typed, but numColNz ignores the bdA option and computes bdB*deg+bdB, contradicting its own doc. With the defaults this under-reserves (e.g. 12 vs 33 for p=2 in 2D): results stay correct, assembly is slower and the public estimate is wrong.

The 3-argument constructor passes x twice instead of y; the types match the original. gsGenericTensorBasis is only included in gismo.h and never used or explicitly instantiated, so it is never instantiated.

The both-unsigned branch returns t2<t2 (always false). The only in-tree callers, util::less/greater in gsBasis.hpp, compare index_t with unsigned, so only the mixed-sign branches run; the unsigned/unsigned path is never reached in-tree.

attributes is std::map<string,string>. All callers pass {{"",""}} or {{"Name",label}}, so testing the value instead of the key only drops an empty-valued attribute such as Name="": no practical difference.

The guard changes from size()>2p+1 to size()>2p, which allows trimming at size 2p+1. Example: inserting 1 into a deg-1 kv {0,1} gives lg=numLeftGhosts()=1 and knot<=*domainBegin(), so trimLeft drops 0. Whether such short knot vectors reach insert() in practice is unclear, and judging it needs the numLeftGhosts/trimLeft semantics from other code.

matchDofs(first.patch, b1, second.patch, b1, i) pairs patch-1 local indices with the same indices on patch 2 and ignores b2 from matchWith. getMapper(conforming) therefore glues the wrong DOFs across every interface.

In innerBoundaries only i_const_iter is typedef'd; b_const_iter is local to boundary(). It would also be a patchSide iterator, which iBegin() cannot initialise. gsMappedBasis<1..3,real_t> is CLASS_TEMPLATE_INST'd, so this is a build break.

inputIndex = m_blockInputPositions(j) replaces the running sum, so with three or more block columns the input slice for block j+1 starts at the wrong row offset. The null-block branch still uses +=, which makes the inconsistency visible.
Only the step number in a gsDebug message changes (i instead of i+1); the computation is unaffected.

'std::vector<T> knots2, knots2;' redeclares a local, which GCC/Clang reject even in an uninstantiated template body. Under the task rule it is 'unsure' because isNested is never called or instantiated anywhere. The variables are unused, so there is no runtime effect.

Both Jacobian rows come from map.first (the same gsFunction<T>* type), so det=0 and the Newton loop would stop at once. However gsTraceLine/gsTraceCurve have no callers (gsPlanarDomain only includes the hpp), so they are never instantiated.

_updateSizeOfCoefs uses the coarse-level index clow on the fine knot vector fkv (both are gsVector<index_t,d>), so fnmb_knts is wrong. That corrupts the size_of_coefs used by THB representBasis/truncation.

In gsPlanarDomain::toMesh (class CLASS_TEMPLATE_INST'd, used by gsView), m_loops[i] uses the y-sample index i instead of the loop index j. That is out of bounds whenever yPoints exceeds the loop count, or picks the wrong loop.

gsKnotVector<T>(0,1,0,ElBlock.PS) is the same constructor as kv[0], but the v-direction Bezier knot vector loses one end multiplicity, so its degree is PS-1 and it no longer matches the (PR+1)(PS+1) coefs. extractBezier is called from gsParaviewUtils.hpp:208. The asymmetry with kv[0] and with the removed kv2(...,PS+1) line shows in the diff.
In the combineCorners branch i==0, so last.push_back(it->second[i]) pushes the first component nrcp times instead of iterating j. allComponents(true) is called in examples/multiGrid_example.cpp:329.

In scaleFrom01(T, gsGeometry<T>&, T, bool), `get` is an undeclared non-dependent name: there is no `using std::get` and no gismo-scope `get`. GCC and Clang reject that at template definition, and the geometry would never get its scaled coefs.

gsTensorBSpline<2,T>(ckv, ckv, coefs) type-checks and is instantiated via CLASS_TEMPLATE_INST gsTHBSplineBasis<2,real_t> in gsTHBSpline_.cpp, but it is wrong (u knots replaced by v knots). getBsplinePatchesToMultiPatch has no caller in the repo at this commit (git grep shows only its declaration and definition).

In the non-template getBoundaries, `size` is undeclared: only patch and side are locals, and no std::size or using-directive is in scope. patchSide(index_t, boxSide/boundary::side, string) has no such argument, so this is a hard compile error, and the side would be lost.

The unary operator-(_expr<E1> const& u) now passes `v`, which is not declared at namespace scope in gsExpressions. As an undeclared non-dependent id it is rejected at definition by GCC and Clang; unary minus on expressions is widely used.

h=(u1-u0)/T(interior) makes the last interior knot equal to u1, which is wrong. But initGraded is never called anywhere in the repo (only its own overload calls it), and gsKnotVector_.cpp explicitly instantiates only gsXml<gsKnotVector<real_t>>, so the member is never instantiated.
target(v0) makes every edge degenerate (source==target). `sharp` is a declared member (gsEdge.h:94), and gsMesh::addEdge calls Edge(v0,v1) (gsMesh.hpp:145).

swap(name1,name2) renames parrays_[second] to name2 (a no-op) and then to name1, so the first property is never renamed and two properties end up named name1. It is reached via gsSurfMesh::swap_vertex_property, used in examples/cc_surf.cpp:331.

starts_with never advances it2 and advances it1 twice, so it compares needle[0] against every other haystack char and can step past end (UB, or a non-terminating loop). It is used in gsOptionList.cpp:286-349.

gsQuadrature::numNodes has only (const gsBasis<T>&, Real, index_t, short_t) and (const gsDomain<T>&, ...) overloads. ab is gsMatrix<T>, so deduction fails when localIntpl is instantiated by gsQuasiInterpolate_.cpp. The bb->ab swap shows against the removed line.
GISMO_UNUSED(x) is static_cast<void>(x) (gsDebug.h:112). Doubling b2 only leaves b1 without an unused-parameter guard (a warning); the function body is GISMO_NO_IMPLEMENTATION anyway.
addCornerValue(boxCorner, T, int p, short_t unknown, int component) receives pIndex as component, so every cv read from XML gets component = patch id, and the parsed cIndex is unused.
`gsMatrix<T> m_box2, m_box2;` redeclares a member and drops m_box1, which gsAffineFunction.hpp:20 initializes. That is a compile error in a widely instantiated class.

m_ops[1]=give(op0) stores the already moved-from (null) op0 and drops op1. However, gsProductOp is not used or explicitly instantiated anywhere in the repo at this commit (git grep finds only gismo.h and the forward declaration).

With = instead of +=, globProjRhs keeps only the last quadrature-point/element contribution, so the L2-projected Dirichlet values are wrong. gsDirichletValuesByL2Projection is called from gsDirichletValues.h:48, and the commented-out line even shows +=.

With l=k the loops write d + d(d+1)/2 entries into prm(sz = d(d+1)/2), which is out of bounds. But deriv2lex_inplace has no caller, and gsFuncData is not explicitly instantiated as a class, so it is never instantiated.

res[i] uses the face-index parameter instead of loop var j, so it writes out of bounds for i >= face size and leaves the other entries uninitialized. faceIndices is called in extensions/gsOpennurbs/gsWriteOpenNurbs.hpp:287 (an optional extension).
splitAt builds right from give(coefL), which was already moved into left, so right gets empty or left coefficients instead of coefR. Same types, so it compiles. splitAt is called by uniformSplit.

In parameterCenter(boxSide), d != dim is always true inside the loop, so the side coordinate is set to the midpoint and dir goes unused (a warning, not an error). It runs as the zero-determinant fallback in computeAuxiliaryData.

it = (lvl==0?1:2) assigns an int to gsKnotVector<T>::uiterator (internal::gsUKnotIterator), which has only an explicit KV constructor and no int assignment. reduceContinuity overrides virtual gsBasis::reduceContinuity, so it is instantiated, and examples call it. Even if it compiled, the loop would never advance.

degreeReduce(j) in the else branch names j, which is only declared in the for loop of the if branch. That is an undeclared non-dependent name in a virtual override, so it is an error. The intended argument is i.
compute() sets out.dim.second twice and never sets dim.first (ParDim). gsFuncData::derivSize, jacobian and hessian read dim.first, so expression evaluation on mapped spline pieces is wrong.
gsVector3d<T>(y,y,z) drops x, so every vertex built from scalars gets x=y. Only an unused-parameter warning.

gd = min(3,pDim) instead of min(3,gDim). For a surface in 3D (pDim 2, gDim 3) the z-coordinate is never written, and for pDim 3 with gDim 1 it reads tmp out of bounds. evaluateMesh is used by gsWriteParaview and gsExprEvaluator.

numColNz multiplies by (1+bdA) instead of (1+bdO), so the bdO option the doc comment describes is ignored and about 2.25x the memory is reserved by default. Results are unaffected; it only changes the memory reservation (and can overflow short_t sooner at high degree).
The x offset uses j instead of i, so patches for different i overlap and the grid is wrong. BSplineCubeGrid is public API, exported via the pybind def_static in gsNurbsCreator_.cpp.
at->side(): no 'at' is declared in computeDirichletDofsIntpl (the loop iterator is 'it'). That is an undeclared non-dependent name in a library-instantiated gsAssembler<T>.

The parameter was renamed to 'map' but the body still uses 'mat', which is undeclared (the member is m_mat), so GCC rejects it at definition. There are no callers of gsAffineFunction::make at this commit.

In the sameElement branch of linearCombination_into, '=' replaces '+=', so only the last active basis function contributes. gsExprAssembler sets SAME_ELEMENT, which reaches gsGeometry::evalAllDers_into, then evalAllDersFunc_into with sameElement=true.
addShift sets m_shift=shift instead of adding, making it identical to setShift. git grep finds no caller of addShift at this commit.
m_end(point1) gives a zero direction, so intersectSegment always returns false. gsParametrization.hpp:616 uses gsLineSegment<2,T>::intersectSegment.

mult = p - multiplicity inserts the knot only up to multiplicity p, but the code (comment 'multiplicity is p+1', it-=p+1, and the coefficient split) assumes p+1. Split geometries get mismatched knots and coefficients. splitAt is used by uniformSplit.
rows = instead of += makes the result only as tall as the last subdomain's rhs, so the following middleRows writes go out of bounds. rhsForSaddlePoint is called in examples/ieti2_example.cpp.

cNew is declared as scalar T in gsMinimalResidual.h, and the diff shows cNew = a0/a1, so cNew.col(0) does not compile. gsMinimalResidual<real_t> is explicitly instantiated in gsMinimalResidual_.cpp. The intended operand is zNew.

The member list now declares cr2 twice (a duplicate member is an error) and drops cr1, which gsMinResQLP.hpp uses (cr1 = -1, MinResQLPSymOrtho(..., cr1, ...)). The class is explicitly instantiated in gsMinResQLP_.cpp.

addTo now overwrites (coeffRef(i,j) = val) instead of accumulating, which contradicts its own 'Add to entry' doc comment. But git grep 'addTo(' at 5178660 finds no gismo caller (only Eigen's unrelated addTo), so the member is never instantiated.

f.getId<gsJITCompilerConfig>(clang) passes the static member function clang where gsFileData::getId(const int&) expects an int, which is ill-formed. But no file includes gsJITCompiler.h at 16725f0 (its include in gismo.h is commented out), so the build would not catch it.
gsBSpline<T>::degreeElevate(short_t i, short_t dir) has no 'j' in scope. The undeclared non-dependent name is rejected at definition time, and gsBSpline is explicitly instantiated in any case.

Using it+degree instead of it+degree+1 gives v=(uIndex(j+p)-uIndex(j))/2. The returned element is still inside the support of function j, which satisfies the gsBasis contract, but it is no longer the middle element, so gsQuasiInterpolate::localIntpl results change.

nextafter(posit y, posit y) declares the same parameter twice and leaves x undeclared, which is a hard error. The function sits under #ifdef gsUniversal_ENABLED, an optional submodule that is off by default, so the default build skips it.
constructBoundaryRep declares only p1; 'p2' is undeclared in that loop. The non-dependent name fails at definition time, and gsMultiPatch<real_t> is explicitly instantiated.

push<...,true>(rowVar, colVar, ra, ra) passes ra where ca belongs, and push uses ca in colInd0(j,ca). In assembleIfc the mirrored side lacks SAME_ELEMENT, so ra and ca differ (0 vs k): the wrong quadrature-point column is used, or it goes out of bounds, whenever m_elim is set.

The signature is _knotIndexToDiadicIndex(level, dir, index_t&). The plant passes the box index i as the direction, while k2 on the next line correctly uses j. This path is reachable through gsHTensorBasis(tbasis, manualLevels=true) and gives wrong directions or out-of-range directions for boxes after the first.
The gsAbsError constructor binds m_f1 to f2, so eval_into computes |f2(u)-f2(geo(u))| and f1 is ignored. gsFieldCreator::absError calls this constructor at line 310.
'index_t i, i;' redeclares i, and j, which the loop 'for (j = 2; ...)' uses, is no longer declared. Both are hard errors in gsLobattoRule<T>::computeReference.

solveUpperTriangular assigns to 'x', but gsGMRes has no member x (its members are tmp, g, g_tmp, h_tmp, y, w) and gsIterativeSolver has none either. The name is undeclared, and the member y that the solution belongs in is never set.

x = step_size * m_update replaces the iterate instead of updating it with +=, while m_res is still updated incrementally. The iterate and the residual become inconsistent and the solver returns a wrong solution.

bndThis = boundaryOffset(bi.second().side(), offset) takes this patch's indices on the other patch's side; the removed line used bi.first(). matchWith therefore matches the wrong dofs whenever the two sides differ, and gsMultiPatch interface code calls it.

'it=4' assigns an int to std::vector<gsVertex<T>*>::const_iterator, and no such conversion exists. writeSingleBasisMesh2D is instantiated through writeSingleBasisMesh (line 224), which gsWriteParaview calls at line 960.

visitedSides is a std::vector<patchSide>, and the plant pushes a patchCorner into it. patchSide has only a default and two-argument constructors, so no conversion exists, and this is a non-template .cpp file.

makeMatrix allocates result(n,n) instead of (n,m). The callers allBoundary and boundaryOffset in gsHTensorBasis pass m=1, so they get an n x n matrix instead of an n x 1 vector (wrong size, and only column 0 is filled).

seg1 = seg % line.size() equals seg, so each segment is compared with itself. identifyCycle then always takes the segment's start point and stores index seg, so it no longer finds the endpoint shared with the next segment and breakCycles splits polylines wrongly.

invertPoints(pr, tmp, accuracy) inverts the parameter-range matrix instead of the point pt; both are gsMatrix<T>, so it compiles. pt is computed and never used, and locatePoints returns wrong patch ids and preimages.
